solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The way to keep head from clonking bed

indicators.note: one piece keeps, or holds, another inside it

parts.note: a path is a way or track

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Advice on stopping your head banging the bed frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetable or flower plot in a garden is called a bed, or equally a small piece of ground.

clue.text: Stuttering king adopts plain type of speech?

indicators.note: speech broken up and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R, for rex, is a king

explanation.surface: A stammering monarch, like George VI, chooses to speak simply.
explanation.definitionFit: An after-dinner speech is given following a meal, so the adjective describes a kind of address.

clue.text: Something of a rake pinches women's threads

indicators.note: grips the next letter between its own

parts.note: a tine is one prong of a rake
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A womaniser who steals ladies' clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake' tempts as a womaniser, but it is the garden tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong string made of twisted strands is a kind of thread, here used in a collective sense.

clue.text: Meat with less lean is a dramatic failure?

parts.note: ham is a meat
meat with less lean is fatter

explanation.surface: A cut of meat with too much fat is a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: An old term for a poor, ranting actor, so a failure on the stage, hence dramatic.

clue.text: Do this and agitate learner driver recklessly?

definitions.text: Do this and agitate learner driver recklessly?

indicators.note: done recklessly, the letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: L is the learner sign on a car

explanation.surface: A warning that driving too close behind a learner will rattle them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recklessly' rearranges AGITATE plus L; the whole clue then describes the act, since following too close is what unnerves the learner ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving dangerously close behind another vehicle is exactly the reckless habit that would fluster a novice motorist.

clue.text: Not quite hiding the source of bitterness in wine

definitions.text: the source of bitterness in wine

indicators.note: not the whole word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a hiding, or beating, is a tanning

explanation.surface: A wine taster who doesn't quite mask the bitter note.
explanation.definitionFit: This astringent compound from grape skins and oak barrels gives red wine its dry, bitter edge.

clue.text: Attention drifting as temperature drops, say

indicators.note: attention that drifts wanders, so the letters are rearranged
the letter is dropped from the word

explanation.surface: Concentration wanders as it gets colder, they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' removes one T from ATTENTION and 'drifting' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter something in a level chanting voice is to say it, a verb sense of the word.

clue.text: A couple start to go around Dutch town

indicators.note: the whole lot is turned around, read backwards

parts.note: a duo is a couple

indicators.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Two people setting out to tour a place in the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The town in South Holland that gives its name to the famous cheese is a Dutch town.

clue.text: Put up with children's quarrel

parts.note: to take something is to put up with it
issue means offspring, children

explanation.surface: Tolerating the children's squabbling.
explanation.definitionFit: To disagree with or challenge someone is an idiom meaning to argue, so quarrel.

clue.text: Giddy time with winos, heading off in skimpy gear

parts.note: a swimming head is a giddy one

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is removed

parts.note: winos are drunks

explanation.surface: A tipsy party of winos turns up in very little clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief shorts worn for bathing are a scanty item of clothing, so skimpy gear describes them.

clue.text: Weirdos, perhaps, absorbed by Yvette's centre parting

indicators.note: taken inside the next piece
the middle letters of the name

parts.note: odd men, strange men, are weirdos

explanation.surface: Odd characters drawn into Yvette's hairdo, perhaps a middle parting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes ET from YVETTE; STRANGE MEN goes inside it. 'parting' looks like hair but means separation.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling-out that drives people apart is a separation, which is a sense of parting.

clue.text: Brief coming before restricting duck hunting

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the next piece inside them
cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: something predating another comes before it in time
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, O

explanation.surface: A legal brief arrives before a ban on duck shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' trims PREDATING to PREDATIN; 'restricting' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that live by preying on others are engaged in hunting, the noun sense of the word.

clue.text: See you in Ibiza having ace parties across island

parts.note: A is the ace in a pack of cards

indicators.note: the first pieces spread across the next, holding it inside

parts.note: dos are parties

explanation.surface: A clubber in Ibiza enjoying great parties all over the island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish farewell is what one would say for goodbye on a Spanish island.

clue.text: Author recited something boring before bed

indicators.note: spoken out, so the letters entered match the sound of the words

parts.note: an awl is a tool for boring holes, followed by a cot, a bed

explanation.surface: A writer reads something dull aloud at bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recited' gives AWL COT said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May Alcott was the American novelist who wrote Little Women.

clue.text: Virus present that might bring on a chill

definitions.text: that might bring on a chill

parts.note: a cold is caused by a virus
to front a show is to present it

explanation.surface: A virus hanging about that could give you a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading edge of a cooler air mass in weather systems brings colder conditions.

clue.text: What might produce 'aero-mist' fancifully?

indicators.note: treated fancifully, the letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: A riddle about which gadget makes a fine spray of mist in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancifully' rearranges AEROMIST; the whole clue also describes what a spray device does.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray nozzle turns liquid into a fine airborne cloud, which is a mist in the air.

clue.text: Protest about short audition for leading lady

indicators.note: the outer word goes around the other

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a trial is an audition or tryout

explanation.surface: A demonstration over a brief tryout for the star role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading lady' suggests an actress, fitting the audition, but here means a woman at the head of a family.
explanation.definitionFit: The woman who heads a family or group is its female leader, a figurative leading lady.

clue.text: West Indian playing guitar hosts unfinished band session

indicators.note: takes the other piece inside
the instrument's name is played with, its letters rearranged
the last letter is left off

parts.note: a jam is an informal session for a band

explanation.surface: A Caribbean guitarist joins in an impromptu jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Indian' suggests the Caribbean but means western India. 'playing' gives GURATI, which 'hosts' JA.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Gujarat, a state in western India, is literally a west Indian.

clue.text: One badger occupying earth when put back in wild state

indicators.note: the whole build is reversed, read from end to start
the pieces sit inside the outer word

parts.note: earth can mean soil or mud
I is the Roman numeral one
to badger is to rile or pester

explanation.surface: A badger living in an earth goes back to its wild existence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' puts IRILE inside MUD, and 'put back' turns MUIRILED round.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenzied, raving excitement or confusion is a wild condition of the mind.

clue.text: Scattered right around in all directions?

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the four compass points S, E, W and N, set in any order

indicators.note: turned around, the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: Things thrown right round in every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark allows the four compass points to be set in any order, rather than an anagram of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Things strewn are spread or thrown untidily about, which is a synonym of scattered.

clue.text: Follow diet at last with a good source of information on GI

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Advice to stick to a diet, from a good gastrointestinal source.
explanation.walkthrough: GI is an American soldier, not the glycaemic index the diet suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal identity disc worn by a US soldier carries his name and details.

clue.text: Answer with almost complete rubbish

indicators.note: nearly all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: full means complete

explanation.surface: A reply that is nearly total nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, rubbish means very poor, which is the sense of dreadful here.

clue.text: Turner oil at Hepworth shows

indicators.note: the words show the letters within them

explanation.surface: Oil paintings by Turner on display at the Hepworth gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter, fitting the Hepworth gallery, but is the machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that spins wood or metal for shaping is a turner, the thing that turns work.

clue.text: Hate to ease up, possessing no time?

indicators.note: the outer word holds the others within it

parts.note: to abate is to lessen or ease up
O, nought, means none
MIN, a minute, is a measure of time

explanation.surface: Someone who loathes having to slow down when short of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something intensely is a direct synonym of hate, the verb.

clue.text: A sweet daughter's round figure

indicators.note: turned round, the letters run backwards

parts.note: pud is short for pudding, a sweet

explanation.surface: A girl's dessert in a round shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reverses PUDD to give DDUP after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To figure is to calculate, and to total a column of numbers is the same thing.

clue.text: Instruction for nose job, perhaps, that requires two pairs of hands

definitions.meaning: an order to shrink the bony ridge of the nose, as a cosmetic surgeon might be told

definitions.text: that requires two pairs of hands
definitions.meaning: a card game played by four people in two partnerships, so four hands are dealt

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is fanciful: the order to make the bony top of the nose smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-known partnership card game is played by four players, each holding a hand of thirteen cards.

clue.text: Vacant attendant serving powerless old prince

indicators.note: emptied, so only the outer letters remain
P, for power, is taken out

parts.note: a serving of food is a helping

explanation.surface: An idle servant waits on a deposed former royal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Anglo-Saxon England this was the title of a royal prince eligible for the throne.

clue.text: Flaming constant punctures on your bike!

indicators.note: the piece pierces the other and sits inside it

parts.note: something flaming is hot
pi is the mathematical constant

explanation.surface: A cyclist cursing yet another flat tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On your bike!' is British slang telling someone to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive British slang phrases meaning clear off, a rude order to leave.
